title: Word 10 — On Death
attribution_note: Word 10 of 28 in the collection Short Moral-Instructive Words — see Word 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: Death has great power to move us to repentance. Death is both known and unknown to us. Known, because all of us will die; unknown, because we do not know when, how, or where we will die. The longer we live, the more our life shrinks, and our days grow fewer, and we draw nearer to death — today nearer to it than we were yesterday, and this hour nearer than we were an hour ago. Death walks invisibly behind every one of us, and seizes a man just when he does not expect it. Almost everyone, and especially the healthy and strong, dreams to himself: I still have time to live, my end is not yet in sight, I will gather goods and take my fill of what I have gathered. But then death falls upon him unawares, and all his dreams and plans perish [Psalm 145:5, LXX]. He who promised himself a long life dies quickly. He who wanted to gather riches and grow rich leaves both the world and his own body in the world. So unknown to us is our end, O Christians. The Lover of mankind, caring for us, has kept our end hidden from us, so that we might always be ready for it and remain in true repentance.

sections.heading: What We Carry to Christ's Judgment

pairs.en: With whatever a man departs this world, with that same he will appear at the judgment of Christ. Sinners! Let us think carefully on this and repent, lest we depart into the age to come still bearing our sins, and stand so before the dread judgment seat. The merciful God has promised to show us His grace and mercy, but He has not promised us tomorrow. Let us then attend to this diligently, and rise up from sleep, and, remembering our death, amend ourselves and prepare for our departure, that we may die a blessed death. *“Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord”* [Revelation 14:13].

sections.heading: The Hour the Saints Wept Over

pairs.en: He dies in the Lord who dies in repentance, and faith, and true prayer. That hour is dreadful for everyone. All the saints, looking toward that hour, wept, and so entreated the Lover of mankind to deliver them in that hour. It is astonishing that the saints weep when they look toward that hour, while sinners do not weep, though they see their own brothers dying every day.

Poor sinners! Why do we sleep? Behold, the devil, like a thief, is stealing our salvation. Let us then fix that hour in our memory, and be ready. From the hour of death, a man will be either eternally blessed or eternally destitute. There the doors of eternity open for everyone, and each one will pass into a happy or an unhappy eternity. From that moment a man begins either to live forever or to die forever. Where now are those who lived before us in luxury, and pleasures, and unrepentance? They have departed from this world, and left all their delights behind, and they dwell in their appointed places, awaiting the last judgment, where they will receive in full according to their deeds. Therefore, while that hour has not yet come upon us, let us turn to our God with a pure heart, and be reconciled to Him through repentance and faith, that we may obtain eternal life. Of this the holy apostles exhort and entreat us in their writings: *“Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ's stead, be ye reconciled to God.* *For He hath made Him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in Him”* [2 Corinthians 5:20–21]. Amen.
